name: Google BigQuery
description: Read BigQuery warehouse metadata via a service account: datasets, tables and table schemas

tools.name: list_datasets
tools.description: List the BigQuery datasets in a GCP project (dataset id, friendly name, location, labels)

project_id.description: GCP project id that owns the datasets (e.g. my-analytics-project)

max_results.description: Datasets to return per page (default 50, max 200)

page_token.description: Opaque nextPageToken from a previous page

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the tables and views in one BigQuery dataset (table id, type, creation and expiration times)

project_id.description: GCP project id that owns the dataset

dataset_id.description: Dataset id within the project (e.g. analytics_prod)

max_results.description: Tables to return per page (default 50, max 200)

page_token.description: Opaque nextPageToken from a previous page

tools.name: get_table
tools.description: Get one BigQuery table's metadata and column schema: row count, byte size, partitioning and field types

project_id.description: GCP project id that owns the dataset

table_id.description: Table or view id within the dataset

needs_review: READ-ONLY by design: metadata only, no tool is marked write:true. jobs.query and jobs.insert are deliberately ABSENT this wave: they are POSTs that execute SQL and BILL the customer's project per byte scanned, so query execution needs its own cost-guard and approval design before it ships.

The declared scope is bigquery.readonly. That scope does permit jobs.query, so adding a query tool later would not need a scope change, only the cost guard above. Anything mutating (dataset/table create, delete) would need the wider bigquery scope.

The google_service_account JWT-bearer grant is NOT blind-provable: the shape-proof harness probes the API surface with a dummy bearer, so paths and auth handling are tested but the token exchange with a real service-account key is not. Flagged token_flow_untested in the proof.

The vault type bigquery has testEndpoint: null (it validates the JSON key shape only), so credential activation cannot be verified in the auth service either; the spec test block (GET /bigquery/v2/projects/quoxprobe/datasets) is the only surface check.

project_id is a required INPUT on every tool rather than being read from the service-account key's own project_id. That is deliberate (one key often reads several projects), but it means an agent must be told which project to look at.
numRows and numBytes come back as JSON strings (int64 over the wire), not numbers, so downstream arithmetic has to cast.
